headline: Ward 24 ranks 47th of 50, strong on schools and groceries, weak on environment and trust.
summary:
Ward 24 covers North Lawndale, South Lawndale, Austin and West Garfield Park on Chicago's West Side. It ranks 47th out of 50 wards overall, with a score of 29.61, near the bottom of the citywide list. Its strongest measures cluster around schools, food access and neighborhood institutions. The ward ranks 1st in the city for mapped faith institutions, with 101 of them, and 1st for houses of worship per resident. It also ranks 1st for grocery stores and supermarkets per resident and 1st for per-pupil school spending, at $23,663 per student. Two modeled estimates land near the top as well, for daily leisure time and for how often residents are expected to spend an evening with neighbors.

The weaker numbers point to environmental and social strain. The ward ranks last in the city on the Chicago Environmental Justice Index, the city's measure of cumulative pollution and vulnerability where a higher score means a heavier burden, and last on the related share of residents living in an EJ-designated area. It also ranks last for modeled social trust, for the share of adults reporting frequent mental distress, for how connected people say they feel to their neighborhood, and for highly rated bars, of which the ward has zero. Together, the numbers describe a ward where schools and neighborhood institutions rank strong while the surrounding environment and public-health measures rank near the worst in the city.
reading_the_rankings: A few of these numbers deserve a second look before they settle anything. The 1st-place rank for grocery stores per resident comes from a source that assigns businesses by ZIP code, and ZIP codes don't follow ward lines, so some of that count may really belong to a neighboring ward. The last-place rank on the Environmental Justice Index is allocated from census tracts by area, which assumes residents are spread evenly inside each tract, so where a tract crosses the ward boundary, part of that score may belong to the ward next door instead. The last-place rank for social trust (19 percent) comes from a statistical model built from citywide survey and demographic data. The source itself rates it low confidence, and the model describes what a ward with this area's demographic makeup tends to look like on average, a general pattern rather than something collected from Ward 24 residents directly.

news.headline: 'Missing Middle' Housing Program Breaks Ground On 27 Units In North Lawndale
news.note: The city broke ground on nine three-flats in North Lawndale as part of a 'Missing Middle' affordable housing program, with Ald. Monique Scott speaking at the event.

news.headline: Southside Blooms Expands Its Nationally Renowned Farm-To-Vase Operation To North Lawndale
news.note: A flower-farming nonprofit based in Englewood opened a second, larger location in North Lawndale for its retail and wholesale operations.

news.headline: Mixed-Use 'Lawndale ReDefined' Apartment Building Gets City Council Approval
news.note: The City Council approved zoning for a six-story, 59-unit mixed-income apartment building on a vacant lot in North Lawndale, with most units set aside as affordable.
